issues.body: The gate's target-controlled build scripts/tests run as the runner user and receive RUNNER_TEMP. Rebinding GITHUB_ENV, GITHUB_PATH, GITHUB_OUTPUT, and GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY only hides their original path strings; it does not make the runner-created files inaccessible. Cargo can enumerate the readable `_runner_file_commands` directory (for example by filename prefixes such as `set_env_`, `add_path_`, and `step_summary_`) and append directly to the real files that the runner consumes after the step. In this lane that can poison the following `push` step, where a write-capable GH_TOKEN is introduced. The new self-tests only verify YAML text and absence of `steps.gate.outputs`; they never exercise or disprove this filesystem bypass, so the marquee quarantine claim is unsupported.
issues.fix_hint: Put the target-controlled gate behind an actual isolation boundary that cannot access the host runner command-file directory (for example, a container with only the required target inputs mounted), or otherwise implement and adversarially test a trusted mechanism that prevents writes to the real runner command files. Add a test using gate-shaped target code that searches RUNNER_TEMP for the original command files and attempts to poison a later sentinel step; approval requires that attempt to fail.
issues.title: Environment-variable redirection does not quarantine same-user runner command files

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The transcript purge is carefully fail-closed and well exercised, but the runner-command-file quarantine does not provide the claimed security boundary. Target-controlled code runs as the runner user and can rediscover the real command files under RUNNER_TEMP, bypassing the substituted environment paths. Because the fix lane subsequently runs a token-bearing push step, this leaves the principal cross-step attack path open.
